5
A micrometer screw gauge is used to measure the diameter of a wire.
The reading on the micrometer with the jaws closed is (–0.05  0.02) mm.
The reading with the wire in position between the two jaws is (+1.03  0.02) mm.
What is the diameter of the wire?
A
(0.98  0.02) mm
B
(1.08  0.02) mm
C
(0.98  0.04) mm
D
(1.08  0.04) mm

hints: Notice the jaws-closed reading is $(-0.05 \pm 0.02)\text{ mm}$ and the reading with the wire is $(+1.03 \pm 0.02)\text{ mm}$ - the first is a negative zero error to be removed.
Recall that true thickness equals observed reading minus zero reading, so you must subtract $-0.05\text{ mm}$ from $1.03\text{ mm}$.
Recall that for addition or subtraction the absolute uncertainties in $\text{mm}$ add, so combine $0.02\text{ mm}$ and $0.02\text{ mm}$ for the final $\pm$ value.
walkthrough: Identify the two micrometer values: zero reading $z = -0.05\text{ mm}$ and wire reading $x = +1.03\text{ mm}$, each with absolute uncertainty $\pm 0.02\text{ mm}$.
State the zero-correction rule: corrected diameter $d = x - z$ because the instrument reads low by $z$ when closed.
Substitute values with units: $d = 1.03\text{ mm} - (-0.05\text{ mm}) = 1.03\text{ mm} + 0.05\text{ mm} = 1.08\text{ mm}$.
Combine uncertainties for a subtraction by adding absolute uncertainties: $\Delta d = 0.02\text{ mm} + 0.02\text{ mm} = 0.04\text{ mm}$.
Write the result as $(1.08 \pm 0.04)\text{ mm}$ with the same decimal places and check the unit is $\text{mm}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: This adds the $-0.05\text{ mm}$ zero reading instead of subtracting it, giving $1.03 - 0.05 = 0.98\text{ mm}$, and it also fails to combine uncertainties.

B.explanation: This gives the correct $1.08\text{ mm}$ value but keeps only $\pm 0.02\text{ mm}$, forgetting that absolute uncertainties add when two readings are subtracted.

C.explanation: This correctly adds uncertainties to $\pm 0.04\text{ mm}$ but uses $1.03 + (-0.05) = 0.98\text{ mm}$, which applies the $-0.05\text{ mm}$ zero error with the wrong sign.

D.explanation: Corrected diameter is $1.03 - (-0.05) = 1.08\text{ mm}$ with combined uncertainty $0.02 + 0.02 = 0.04\text{ mm}$.
